newsitem.title: USA: Analysts delighted with WorldCom figures.
newsitem.headline: Analysts delighted with WorldCom figures.

text.p: WorldCom Inc has had long experience of integrating acquisitions successfully, but it has pulled off its most difficult coup with sparkling results from its debut quarter combined with MFS Communications Co.
Analysts were delighted that the combined company on Thursday substantially exceeded consensus estimates for fourth quarter results, excluding one-time merger costs.
"This was a spectacular quarter with several upside surprises," said Linda Meltzer of UBS Securities. "This is a terrific platform for accelerating growth in 1997," she added.
WorldCom's fourth quarter earnings per share excluding merger costs were $0.29 per share, up from $0.20 a year ago.
"That's two or three cents better than estimates," said Robert Waldman, an analyst at Salomon Bros.
WorldCom bought MFS in August in a $14 billion stock swap, announced just after MFS had bought Internet service company UUNET for $2 billion.

WorldCom did well from the emerging competition in U.S. and international telecommunication markets where it has been acting as a carrier of traffic to aggressive long distance resellers like Excel Communications Inc.
Resellers are eating into the market share of the established companies like AT&T Corp, and are increasingly able to provide sophisticated services using networks like WorldCom's.
In addition WorldCom is winning business to carry traffic for the regional Bells out of their local calling regions as they position themselves to enter the long distance market.
Meltzer's forecasts were at the high end of Wall Street estimates, and she said they may now prove conservative.
"The real standout was MFS, which generated positive cashflow for the full quarter," Meltzer said.
Analysts were impressed that the strength of the WorldCom results came during the fourth quarter, which is seasonally weak for phone companies in the business market.

They were also impressed that the results do not yet include the economies and savings from putting WorldCom's long distance network together with MFS's business local calling networks, which will boost results later this year.
Meltzer expects WorldCom to reap $350 million of savings in the first year and $800 million in total.
